# Toast

A short message that confirms an action and goes away.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill">In Multi-brand</span></p>

## See it live

<div class="odv-live"><span class="odv-wait">Start Storybook to see it live: <code>npm run storybook</code></span><iframe src="http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=components-toast--examples&viewMode=story&globals=scheme:multi-brand--aster;mode:light" title="Toast examples in Storybook" loading="lazy"></iframe><div class="bar"><span>Live from Storybook</span><a href="http://localhost:6006/?path=/docs/components-toast--docs">Open Toast in Storybook</a><a href="http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=components-toast--examples&viewMode=story&globals=scheme:multi-brand--aster;mode:dark">See it in dark</a></div></div>

## When to use it

**In Multi-brand:** Confirms a saved change.

- **Use it when:** Saved, sent, exported: something people should notice without stopping.
- **Not when:** A failure people must understand (alert or dialog), or a notice that stays (alert).

Instead:

- [Alert](./alert.md): Stays on the page.
- [Dialog](./dialog.md): Needs an answer.

## How Multi-brand uses it

<div class="odv-grid two"><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">The words of an error</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> Shared across brands: plain and specific</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> Brand tone in errors</div></div><div class="cap">Errors read the same in every brand, so support can help anyone. Example: “Your card was declined. Try another card or contact your bank.”</div></div><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">A success message</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> Brand tone allowed: Aster calm, Birch friendly, Coral upbeat</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> The same flat line in every brand</div></div><div class="cap">Success is a safe moment for brand tone. Example: “Aster: Your plan is active. · Birch: You're all set! · Coral: Let's go, your plan is live.”</div></div></div>

## Why it works this way

Toast looks the way it does because of 3 answers about this product. Each card is one answer, in three steps: the answer, what it decided for Toast, and what would move if it changed.

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-voice-definition"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>How is the voice defined?</b><code>voice.definition</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">A shared core, brand tone on top</div><p>Errors and confirmations are shared; brand tone sits on top.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Toast</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>neutral</b>: A shared line with brand words.</span></li><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>danger</b>: Shared across brands: plain and specific.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Alert: destructive</code> <code>Empty: default</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">2</div><small>Toast decisions would reopen</small><p>No other answer follows from it.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-voice-count"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>How many tones does it use?</b><code>voice.count</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">One per brand</div><p>A shared core, with a tone per brand.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Toast</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>success</b>: Brand tone allowed: Aster calm, Birch friendly, Coral upbeat.</span></li></ul></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">1</div><small>Toast decision would reopen</small><p>No other answer follows from it.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-voice-values"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>How does it sound?</b><code>voice.values</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Plain and direct</div><p>The shared core is plain and direct.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Toast</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>danger</b>: Shared across brands: plain and specific.</span></li></ul></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">1</div><small>Toast decision would reopen</small><p>No other answer follows from it.</p></div></div></section>

## Words

- Shared structure: object, state, next step.
- Brand tone lives in headlines and marketing copy, not in errors.
- Errors and confirmations read the same in every brand.
- Use: Get started, Plan, Order. Avoid: Brand-specific words in errors, Jargon.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Save
- `content.action.cancel`: Cancel
- `content.action.destroy`: Remove
- `content.action.retry`: Try again
- `content.action.empty-action`: Get started

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

Test before you ship:

- [ ] It is announced politely without taking focus, and stays long enough to read. undefined
- [ ] Nothing people must act on lives only in a toast. undefined

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add toast
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.
